label: input x at original positions 2-4
explanation: Token-and-position feature: fires when the input token is the letter x during the original phase at positions t=2, 3 or 4. Every such step activates (dev precision 1.0, F1 0.98). Activations are strongest for x at t=2-3, e.g. 3rd/4th token (top examples have x at t=3, ~0.98-1.0 of max). Activations are weaker at t=4, and lowest-quartile examples are x at t=4 following digits or repeated tokens. A small number of weak activations happen for x at t=1 (rate 0.3%, ~0.2% of mass). It never fires on x at t=0 or t>=5, on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (12 negligible exceptions). It is somewhat stronger when this is the first x in the sequence.

issues: Minor: the t=1 activations are not spread evenly. x at t=1 fires on 9.8% of occurrences (test precision 0.098), mostly when the first token is o, t or x. They carry only 0.23% of activation mass and all sit in the lowest quartile, so this is a weak secondary pattern and does not change the label.
Minor: the explanation's '0.3%' is the active rate over all t=1 steps, not over x-at-t=1 steps. The per-x rate is about 9.8%.

Checked and confirmed: test precision 1.0, recall 0.966, F1 0.983, mass recall 0.998. No false positives on the test split. Every miss is a weak x-at-t=1 activation (about 0.03-0.06 of max). Zero activations on any non-x token or on the delimiter, and none at t=0 or t>=6. The 12 copy-phase activations are at t=5 (recall_idx 2, L=3). x at t=5 in the original phase never fires (precision 0). Mass is about 0.40 at t=2, 0.46 at t=3 and 0.13 at t=4, which supports the stated magnitude ordering.
Adding t=1 (t in 1..4) lowers test F1 to 0.865, so the original predicate is the better boundary.
